title: Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

reading.body:
This is a fabrication failure aimed at a specific person rather than a false statement about the world. Photographs taken from a woman's private social media account were used to generate explicit images of her, and the resulting material depicts a real, identifiable individual in acts that never occurred. The harm does not depend on anyone believing a claim, because the images are the claim.

The distribution ran through consumer platforms rather than any single AI product. Fake accounts on Instagram, Discord and Facebook, set up with several Gmail addresses, carried the images to audiences the victim never chose. Detection came from anonymous Instagram messages telling her the material was circulating on Discord servers, which means the platforms did not surface it to her first. Catching this earlier would have required either matching the generated images back to the source photographs or linking the separate fake accounts to one operator, and neither link was made before the content spread.

What is not established is the specific AI tool used, and the case rests on an arrest and a continuing investigation rather than a conviction. The stated motive comes from the man's own admission as reported by police, not from a court finding.

reports.title: Delhi: Man held for circulating obscene AI-generated photos of college acquaintance
Resentment leads techie to circulate fake obscene images of woman online

summary:
A 22-year-old man named Keshav Bansal was arrested in Delhi for creating and distributing artificial intelligence-generated obscene images of a college acquaintance. Bansal, a BTech graduate in Electronics and Communication Engineering from East Punjabi Bagh, obtained photographs from the woman's private social media account and used AI technology to generate explicit morphed images. He then shared this content through multiple fake accounts on Instagram, Discord, and Facebook, using several Gmail addresses to hide his identity.

The 22-year-old victim discovered the offensive material when she received messages from anonymous Instagram accounts informing her that her morphed photographs and videos were circulating on Discord servers. She reported the harassment to the Cyber Police Station in North Delhi. During the investigation, police analyzed digital footprints and traced the fake profiles back to Bansal. He admitted that personal resentment from college had motivated his actions. Police recovered a mobile phone, two SIM cards, and other digital evidence related to the case, and investigation is continuing.
